open_questions: Modest transit-to-transit depth scatter (chi2 10.56 dof 3 p 0.014, near gap p_chance 0.02329) should be verified with higher-SNR follow-up to confirm achromatic depth stability.
No centroid_all measurement yet; ground-based time-series photometry can confirm the transit is on the target given centroid inconclusive.
dossier.public_summary: The 13.6-day 3.3 Earth-radius dip on this K-dwarf is flat-bottomed, the right duration for the star, and shows no odd-even or secondary eclipse. No nearby star can make the dip and the small apparent depth change lines up with different pipelines. The star is spotted and variable, which weakens the machine-score, but a planet remains the best explanation.

reasons.why: Flat bottom favours a planet over a V-shaped eclipsing binary or grazing event.
Planet-sized (3.3 Rearth) with duration ratio 0.8801 matching stellar density (fit_log_density_ratio 0.1536); stellar radius consistent across TIC/FLAME/GSPPhot.
No significant odd/even difference and no reliable secondary eclipse, inconsistent with an eclipsing binary at twice the period.
reasons.value: odd_even diff_sigma 1.426, secondary snr 2.814, odd/even depths 1549/1167 ppm

reasons.why: No neighbour within one TESS pixel can plausibly cause the dip with <=25% eclipse; apparent depth change between sectors is N=2, one QLP and one SPOC, so attributed to pipeline calibration, not intrinsic variability.
reasons.value: plausible_within_1px 0, centroid verdict inconclusive, sectors p_constant 0.02066, sector_depths_by_source verdict steady

reasons.why: Large spot amplitude and modest phase-curve signal on a spotted M-dwarf (Teff 3981K) explain high xgboost planet_rank 0.08 and transit_depths p_consistent 0.014; pattern is common for planets around spotted stars and alone does not indicate a binary when shape is planetary.
